Create the cover illustration for an illustrated book of modern fairy tales, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: In a snowy farmyard at the very end of a narrow valley, the Suitor has just stepped out of his small car and stands looking up at an old white farmhouse with peeling paint, its roof patched with a big blue tarpaulin. At the kitchen window, three faces crowd together to peer out at him: the Farmer, the Farmer's Wife and the Daughter in her new green beanie. Pale late-winter sun and blue shadows.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Suitor: A tall, gangly man of about twenty-seven with a round, eager face, apple-pink cheeks, a small blunt nose, hopeful pale-blue eyes, a nervous smile and neat butter-blond hair parted in the middle and combed down flat, except for one unruly cowlick at the back. He wears his best date outfit: a slightly too short cinnamon-brown corduroy blazer over a white shirt buttoned to the top, grey chinos and polished black boots, with a small brown leather shoulder bag.
- the Farmer: A big, burly, barrel-chested farmer of about fifty-five with a broad, ruddy face, a small snub nose, twinkling little blue eyes, bushy brown eyebrows, a shock of unruly brown hair and a long brown beard that splits into two scraggly forks. He wears a faded, pilled dusty-red wool jumper with one brand-new sleeve knitted in almost the same red, only brighter and crisper, while the old sleeve has a hole at the elbow, patched work trousers and thick grey wool socks.
- the Farmer's Wife: A small, wiry, bustling woman of about fifty with a narrow, freckled face, a long pointed nose, bright little grey eyes, a busy, pursed mouth and frizzy ginger hair escaping from a big brown hair clip. She wears a faded grey-blue fleece, mud-brown corduroy trousers and an apron. On her right foot is one brand-new, spotless white trainer; on her left foot, an old, scuffed grey one.
- the Daughter: A cheeky young woman of about twenty-five with a long face, a sharp chin, a snub, upturned nose, big round brown eyes, rosy cheeks, a little rosebud mouth and thick black hair in two short, stiff plaits that poke straight out to the sides. She wears a faded brown hoodie and old grey jeans, and on her head a brand-new, bright emerald-green knitted beanie with a big fluffy white pom-pom.

Story world: Present-day Norway in late winter. The farm kitchen is small and worn smooth: a scrubbed pine table with mismatched chairs and two stools, a wood-burning stove, a rag rug on cracked linoleum, a coffee pot and a plate of sweet buns. Everything is old and faded except the family's three new things: the farmer's one new sleeve, the wife's one new trainer and the daughter's new beanie. The suitor carries a small brown leather shoulder bag.

This story's season, light and colours: Late winter at the end of a narrow valley: old grey snow, blue shadows and a pale, low sun. Inside the kitchen, warm light from the stove and a hanging lamp on faded pine and worn linoleum, from which the three new things shine out: a bright red sleeve, a spotless white trainer and an emerald-green beanie.
